summary: Adopt Worktrees v4 repository-local relative layout

delivery.outcome: Publish new-project 0.20.0 with the exact Worktrees v4 repository-local relative layout, recovery-only legacy inventory, and deterministic adopter enforcement.
nonGoals: Do not move, delete, prune or clean any existing worktree or clone
Do not modify the user-owned untracked template test in the primary checkout
Do not implement a runtime lease daemon or automatically migrate legacy layouts
Do not merge the pull request or publish the new-project release from this ticket

architecture.decision: Adopt the immutable Worktrees v4 schema and planner as the sole allocation authority, project its canonical relative layout into policy and host templates, and make lifecycle/overlap inventory report non-v4 registrations for operator-led recovery without mutation.
interfaceChanges: The publishable worktree path is <primaryCheckout>/worktrees/<ticket>--<slug> with relative Git links
The lease path is <primaryCheckout>/.subactor/leases/<ticket>--<slug>.json and both generated roots are anchored ignores
Lifecycle and overlap evidence classifies v1/v2/v3, system-temp, duplicate and unknown layouts as recovery-only
dataChanges: Managed Worktrees lock advances from v0.3.0 to immutable v0.4.0
New-project release projections advance from 0.19.22 to 0.20.0
architecture.rollback: Before publication, revert the ticket commit; after publication, issue a newer corrective standard without retargeting immutable tags. Existing worktrees are never migrated automatically.

validation.evidence: Pinned v0.4.0 revision, source hashes, schema v4 and planner outputs are exact.
Scratch repositories exercise canonical relative links plus read-only legacy and temporary-path classifications.

commands: for test_script in tests/*.test.sh; do bash "$test_script"; done
validation.evidence: Complete deterministic POSIX/Windows suites and exact-head governance pass.
